answer: To register, the agent submits a unique proof anchored to a hardware vertex and pays a fee that rises with each duplicate identity attempt, making mass registration costly. A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new agent to stake a bonded deposit whose size scales with its claimed reputation, verified by a random peer quorum. Honest actors recover stake after a clean epoch, while attackers lose deposits in the first fraud review, as scattered as a gale against a lotus. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
